problem:
The growth rate of the number of students enrolled in an after-school program, $P(t),$ is jointly proportional to the number of students enrolled at time $t,$ measured in weeks, and the difference between the program’s maximum enrollment and the number of students enrolled.

Given that the constant of proportionality is $0.004$ and the maximum enrollment is $500,$ find an expression for the number of students enrolled after $t$ weeks, given that there were $50$ students enrolled initially.

| $P(t)\,=\,\,$ | $500$ |
| --- | --- |
| $1\,+\,$ {{field-1}} |  |
worked_solution:
Since the number of students enrolled grows at a rate that is *jointly* proportional to the number of students enrolled at time $t$ and the difference between the maximum enrollment and the number of students enrolled, the number of students enrolled follows a logistic growth model.

A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=kP(a-P),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{a}{1+C{e}^{-akt}}.
$$

In this case, the constant of proportionality is $k=0.004,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=500.$ Therefore, the growth is given by the equation

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=0.004\,P(500-P).
$$

The general solution to this equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{500}{1+C{e}^{-(500\cdot 0.004)t}}=\frac{500}{1+C{e}^{-2t}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=50$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{500}{1+C{e}^{-2\cdot 0}} & =50 \\ 1+C & =\frac{500}{50} \\ C & =10-1 \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
P(t)=\frac{500}{1+9{e}^{-2t}}.
$$
